causes.rule: For an id with two or more rows in one portfolio group, every row of that id (inside the group and across all its groups) carries the same value on each of the 15 readable columns other than portfolio_group: the four dates, action, transaction_type, transaction_sub_type, external_flow, asset_id, asset_name, cusip, _source_file, _ingested_at and as_of_date. Re-apply: group the rows by transaction_id and portfolio_group; take the set of the 15-column tuples over the group's rows; the set has size 1. Tested on every one of the 590 ids: 590 of 590 satisfy it, and 2337 of 2337 (id, group) pairs. Nothing readable tells the copies apart, including the load stamp and source file.
causes.dedupe_on_id_alone: cannot tell without a money column
causes.dedupe_on_id_alone_why: If the copies are the same transaction re-sent, keeping one is correct; if they are separate legs or lots that differ only in units, price or amount (money or account columns this read may not see), keeping one drops a real row. Nothing on the 15 readable columns separates the two readings.

unexplained.why: none: all 590 ids sit under the one cause. What stays NOT_ESTABLISHED is not an unplaced id but what the cause means: whether the same-group copies also match on the money columns (units, price, market value, fees, income) and the account columns, which this read may not see. Only a read of those columns can say whether they are re-sent copies or real separate rows.
